cards.text: Welcome to Mags' station, friend, where the words ring out LOUD. Jesus is traveling through the towns and villages, teaching as He makes His way toward Jerusalem. Then someone asks Him whether only a few people will be saved.

cards.question: Jesus doesn't give that person a head count. Instead He tells them to make every effort to enter through what?
Jesus says many will try to enter through that narrow door and will not be able.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells His listeners what's coming. The master of the house shuts the door, and they'll be the ones standing outside knocking, saying, "Lord, open the door for us."

cards.question: The door is shut and the people outside are knocking. What does the master of the house tell them?

answers.text: I do not know where you are from
Come back again in the morning
Wait there until I call for you

cards.text: So the folks outside pull out their résumé: we ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets. Friend, that's like asking for the corner office because you once waved at the boss in the parking lot.

cards.question: Once the people outside remind the master that they ate and drank with him, he opens the door and lets them in.

cards.text: The master doesn't budge: "I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers." And Jesus says there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

cards.question: Jesus says the ones thrown out will see some familiar faces inside the kingdom of God. Who will they see?

answers.text: Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets
Moses and Aaron and Miriam and all the priests
David and Solomon and Hezekiah and all the kings

cards.text: Then Jesus mentions a table in the kingdom of God, and friend, you KNOW this old stamper just leaned all the way in.

cards.question: Jesus says people will come and recline at the table in the kingdom of God. Where will they come from?
Jesus sums it up by saying some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.

cards.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees come to Jesus. They're a strict group in the Jewish religion (Acts 26:5), and what they say has to do with Herod, the ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1).

cards.question: The Pharisees tell Jesus to leave and get away because Herod wants to kill Him.

cards.text: Friend, I jump when my oven timer DINGS. Jesus hears that Herod wants Him dead, and He just says, "Go tell that fox," then gives the fox a message.

cards.question: Jesus sends a message to Herod. What does He say He'll keep doing today and tomorrow?

answers.text: Driving out demons and healing people
Staying out of sight in the villages

cards.text: Jesus isn't running, friend. His message for Herod ends with, "on the third day I will reach My goal."

cards.question: Jesus says He must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, because it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to the city itself: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her..." I don't know about you, friend, but I hear heartbreak in that.

cards.question: Jesus says He has often longed to gather Jerusalem's children together. What does He compare it to?

answers.text: A hen gathering her chicks under her wings
A shepherd gathering his sheep into the fold
A fisherman gathering his nets into the boat

cards.question: Jesus says Jerusalem was willing to be gathered together.

cards.text: Nope. In Jesus' words, "you were unwilling!" Then He says, "Look, your house is left to you desolate."

cards.question: Jesus tells Jerusalem they won't see Him again until they say something. What will they say?

answers.text: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord
Truly this was the Son of God
We have no king but Caesar
